Title: Supply Chain Data Analyst
Description:
Bevi is on a mission to transform how beverages are delivered and consumed. Our connected beverage platform eliminates the need for single-use bottles and cans, making it easy, fun, and sustainable to stay hydrated. As the category leader in IoT-enabled beverage technology, we're building a future where Bevi machines are everywhere people live, work, and connect. We've raised over $160M in venture capital, serve thousands of customers across the US, Canada, UK and Ireland, and we've been rapidly growing year over year, saving over 1 billion bottles from waste. In addition to driving hypergrowth with our current product line, Bevi is heavily investing in new product development.

The Supply Chain Data Analyst will play a critical role in evolving Bevi’s operational efficiency by managing the tactical procurement of components while simultaneously auditing and modernizing our core supply chain workflows. This role serves as a hybrid practitioner and internal consultant, bridging the gap between current manual purchasing processes and a future state powered by automation, seamless system integration, and AI. Operating with a blend of extreme detail orientation and technical aptitude, you will partner with Global Supply Managers (GSMs) and cross-functional teams to ensure data integrity, identify bottlenecks, and propose scalable solutions. This is a high-impact opportunity to influence how a high-growth hardware startup leverages emerging technology to scale its supply chain and master data operations.

Key Responsibilities


Tactical PO Execution: Partner with the Planning and Global Supply Management (GSM) team to execute day-to-day purchasing, managing PO issuance, tracking delivery schedules, and handling routine expedites to align with production needs.
Invoice & Receiving Resolution: Act as the first line of defense for tactical discrepancies, investigating and correcting data when vendor shipments or invoices do not match ERP records.
Master Data Governance: Take ownership of SKU and BOM accuracy, acting as the gatekeeper for our "single source of truth" across core platforms (e.g., NetSuite, Arena) .
Process Mapping & Documentation: Lead the discovery of "current state" procurement workflows, identifying manual handoffs and creating visual maps or SOPs to standardize supply chain operations.
Automation Opportunity Assessment: Analyze documented purchasing and inventory processes to identify repetitive tasks ripe for automation using tools like Zapier, Workato, or native ERP functionalities.
AI Implementation Research: Investigate and pilot AI-driven use cases (such as LLM assisted data cleaning, automated vendor follow-ups, or predictive stock alerting) to reduce administrative overhead.
Continuous Improvement Reporting: Build simple dashboards to track supply chain KPIs (e.g., PO cycle time, on-time delivery) and the "before and after" impact of implemented process changes.


Qualifications


Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Analytics, Industrial Engineering, Information Systems, or 1-3 years of equivalent practical experience.
Strong analytical mindset with an obsession for detail and a knack for "connecting the dots" between master data, procurement execution, and downstream business functions.
Proficiency in ERP systems (NetSuite preferred) and PLM software (Arena), alongside advanced Excel/Google
Sheets skills (Pivot Tables, VLOOKUPs/XLOOKUPs). Exposure to or high interest in automation platforms, process mapping tools (e.g., Lucidchart, Miro), and AI tools (ChatGPT/Claude for work, API basics, or low-code environments).
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate "supply chain pain" into clear technical requirements for engineering and finance stakeholders.
A self-starter attitude with the instinct to fix the root cause of data errors or slow processes, rather than just treating the symptoms in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.


What Success Looks Like


Operational Stability: Consistent, accurate execution of all buyer responsibilities with a visible reduction in "fire drills" caused by data silos or manual handoffs.
Improved Data Integrity: Maintenance of a highly accurate "single source of truth" within our primary systems (NetSuite/Arena) that perfectly mirrors GSM-negotiated terms.
Comprehensive Process Library: Delivery of a centralized repository of documented core procurement and master data workflows that are easy for the team to navigate and update.
Measurable Efficiency Gains: Successful implementation of at least 2-3 automation or AI assisted "quick wins" that reduce manual data entry or administrative work hours for the supply chain team.


At Bevi, We Believe Compensation Is a Powerful Tool To Attract, Retain, And Grow Talent. Our Compensation Philosophy Centers On 5 Principles


Market-driven - We anchor pay decisions in real-time market data
Performance-based - We reward individual impact, not just tenure
Equitable - We ensure fairness across teams, roles, and demographics
Growth-focused - We invest in talent that scales with Bevi
Total Rewards approach - We strategically balance base pay, bonuses, benefits, and equity


The posted compensation range reflects the salary* for this position. Some roles may be eligible for a commission plan or a bonus incentive. All Bevi employees receive equity in the form of stock options. All full-time employees are invited to participate in our Total Rewards plan, which includes health & medical benefits, flexible spending accounts, flexible PTO, and more. Offers to join Bevi are based on a few criteria, including the scope of the role, the candidate's work experience, targeted skills, internal equity of the team, and external market data.


For Sales roles: The posted range reflects base salary plus commission which is the total potential on target earnings (OTE) for the position.


Pay Range

$76,585—$94,605 USD

Benefits


Comprehensive medical, dental and vision insurance plans with BlueCross BlueShield, 95% paid by employer
401(k) with company match
Flexible PTO plus 12 company holidays, and additional paid days for sick leave, etc
Generous fully paid parental leave for both birth parents and non-birth parents
Fully employer paid disability and life insurances
Wellness and fitness reimbursements
Monthly stipends for cell phone use and commuting costs
Onsite snacks, weekly catered lunch, and (of course) unlimited Bevi ... plus composting and terra-cycling, too
Happy hours, team-building events, bagel breakfasts, Values awards - and more.


A note on AI in our hiring process: We use AI to help synthesize interview notes and surface themes from feedback, keeping our process consistent as we grow. Every application is reviewed by a member of our team, and interviews may be recorded to support note-taking, just let us know if you'd prefer we don't. We'll also ask how you're learning and experimenting with AI in your work. Growing our AI fluency is something every Bevi team member is committed to and invested in.

Our commitment to responsible innovation is reflected in our partnership with the Mass AI Coalition, a collaboration that aligns with our dedication to community-driven progress and the future of technology.

We're passionate about supporting career growth and would love to be part of your professional journey. We also know that talent comes in many forms. We value individual accomplishments, specialized knowledge, and genuine passion over simply checking boxes on a requirements list. Whether you're a seasoned expert or an emerging talent, we're looking for people who are ready to build what's next. If any of our open positions interest you, we'd encourage you to apply! A member of the Bevi Talent team 'recruiting@bevi.co' will be reaching out about next steps if we would like to move forward.

Accommodations

Bevi is committed to an inclusive hiring process and we aim to provide accommodations for persons with disabilities. If you need any accommodations for the application or throughout the interview process please contact recruiting@bevi.co.

Title: SIOP Data Analyst - Direct Hire
Description:
Senior Data Analyst

Department: Office of the COO

Reports To: SIOP Manager

Location: Full‑time Onsite — MetroWest Boston Area

Schedule: 5 days onsite (future potential for 4 onsite / 1 remote)

Target Salary Range: $80,000 – $120,000




About the Company (Disguised)

Our client is a leading provider of advanced manufacturing and automation solutions, operating multiple technology centers across North America. The organization specializes in custom machining systems, automation integration, and turnkey production solutions, supporting a wide range of industrial and high‑precision manufacturing customers.

Position Summary

The Senior Data Analyst is a key analytical partner within the Office of the COO, responsible for transforming complex operational, sales, and service data into strategic insights that drive business performance. This role leads the development of enterprise dashboards, reporting frameworks, and data models that support SIOP, sales operations, and aftermarket service functions.

The analyst collaborates closely with cross‑functional leaders to deliver data‑driven recommendations that enhance revenue growth, operational efficiency, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the collection, integration, and analysis of data from CRM, ERP, and enterprise systems to support sales performance, aftermarket services, and SIOP planning cycles.
Design and maintain advanced dashboards and KPI reports across equipment sales, service revenue, parts consumption, and forecasting accuracy.
Serve as the primary analytics partner for SIOP, providing demand/supply analysis, forecast variance reporting, and scenario modeling for executive decision‑making.
Develop standardized aftermarket analytics, including service contract utilization, customer lifecycle metrics, and parts‑usage trends.
Perform complex statistical analyses to identify trends, patterns, and opportunities for operational and revenue optimization.
Ensure data integrity and governance through rigorous validation, documentation, and quality‑assurance practices.
Collaborate with Sales, Operations, Finance, and Aftermarket teams to translate business needs into scalable, automated reporting solutions.

Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About The Team

The People Analytics team is at the forefront of transforming how we understand and optimize our workforce. We are a dynamic group of analytical thinkers and storytellers who leverage advanced analytics and robust methodologies to create strategic insights from complex HR data. Collaborating closely with HR Business Partners, Program Management Teams, Business Operations, Talent Acquisition and various cross functional stakeholders we provide actionable insights that drives informed decisions across the entire employee lifecycle; from optimizing talent acquisition and development to enhancing engagement and retention. Our work directly shapes a thriving employee experience, fuels organizational growth, and ensures our people strategy is truly data-driven.

About The Job

The People Data Analyst owns the reporting and data quality foundation that enables our People Analytics team to deliver insights across Talent Acquisition and People Operations. You'll write the SQL, maintain the dashboards, run audits, and fulfill the ad hoc requests that keep our stakeholders informed and our data trustworthy.

This role is ideal for an early-career analyst who thrives on precision, wants deep exposure to HR data systems end-to-end, and is looking to build the technical muscle that underpins a career in people analytics. You'll work closely with our Senior Analysts — learning how upstream data work translates into downstream strategy while owning your own deliverables from day one.

Provide critical support to the Senior People Data Analysts by executing standard data runs, owning reporting requests, and maintaining operational continuity across both TA and People Ops domains.

Maintain, troubleshoot, and perform minor enhancements on existing dashboards to ensure they remain accurate, functional, and up to date.

Hands-on experience navigating and utilizing business intelligence tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI, Looker) for data visualization and report generation.

Familiarity with HR systems and data structures (e.g., Greenhouse ATS, Gem CRM, Rippling, Workday).

Title: Data Science Analyst, Equity Research, Healthcare Team
Description:
About Us

Wellington Management offers comprehensive investment management capabilities that span nearly all segments of the global capital markets. Our investment solutions, tailored to the unique return and risk objectives of institutional clients in more than 60 countries, draw on a robust body of proprietary research and a collaborative culture that encourages independent thought and healthy debate. As a private partnership, we believe our ownership structure fosters a long-term view that aligns our perspectives with those of our clients.

About The Role

THE POSITION

We are looking for a Data Science Analyst (Science Analyst) to join the Healthcare team within Global Investment Research. With over $100B invested in healthcare, across over 50 Portfolio Managers, this represents a flagship franchise for Wellington. The Healthcare team invests globally across the full healthcare continuum, including Biopharma, Healthcare Services and Medical Technology. The Healthcare team includes over 10 colleagues.

The Science Analyst will work as an integral team member alongside Global Industry Analysts and Portfolio Managers, helping identify where data science, AI and alternative data can create differentiated investment insight across the healthcare sector (MedTech, Pharmaceuticals, Biotech, Healthcare Services). The ideal candidate brings hands-on experience in an investment setting, strong Python, SQL and AI skills, sound judgment for turning messy inputs into outputs the team can act on, and a genuine interest in the healthcare sector and the companies operating within it. They should be comfortable working independently, setting their own priorities, and moving fluidly between deep dataset work and quick-turnaround requests.

Responsibilities

Responsibilities for this position will include the following:


Work as an integral part of the Healthcare team, partnering directly with Global Industry Analysts and Portfolio Managers.
Translate broad investment questions into testable data science workflows and analytical outputs.
Apply AI and agentic tools to streamline research workflows and contribute directly to investment idea generation.
Communicate results clearly, including limitations, confidence levels, and interpretation risk.
Serve as an experienced data science resource across the Healthcare team's coverage areas.
Rapidly get up to speed on new companies, sub-sectors, datasets, and business models as the need arises.
Assess and sequence incoming requests based on expected investment impact, feasibility, and how repeatable the resulting work would be.
Develop differentiated signals and analytical frameworks from alternative and structured datasets relevant to healthcare investing.
Evaluate dataset quality, coverage, bias, and signal durability.
Build repeatable tools, screens, and research outputs that can be used across companies and themes within the sector.
Partner with Data Engineering to productionize high-value signals where appropriate.



Qualifications

Ideal candidates will have:


3-5+ years of experience in data science, alternative data, investment research, healthcare analytics, or a related analytical role.
Prior experience working with investment teams, research teams, or senior business stakeholders.
Strong Python and SQL skills.
Comfort with AI/LLM tooling and agentic workflows, and the ability to apply them to streamline the research process and support idea generation.
Experience working with large, messy, real-world datasets.
Hands-on experience with a variety of alternative datasets, including a track record of sourcing and evaluating new or emerging data, not just working with what's already established.
Strong ability to evaluate dataset quality, bias, representativeness, and signal robustness.
Genuine investment acumen and curiosity about markets, companies, and how data translates into an investment thesis — not just a technical interest in the data itself.
Ability to translate ambiguous investment or business questions into concrete analyses.
Strong communication skills and ability to present nuanced findings to senior stakeholders.
High judgment and comfort operating independently in ambiguous environments.



LOCATION

The Data Science Analyst will ideally be based in Wellington’s Global Headquarters in Boston, MA. Location in the New York, NY office will also selectively be considered.

Not sure you meet 100% of our qualifications? That’s ok. If you believe that you could excel in this role, we encourage you to apply and welcome a chance to review your background. We are dedicated to building and maintaining a diversified workforce and considering a broad array of candidates with a variety of skill, workplace experiences, and backgrounds.

As an equal opportunity employer, Wellington Management ensures that all qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, religion, creed, national origin, age, ancestry, disability (physical or mental), medical condition, citizenship, marital status, pregnancy, veteran or military status, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. If you are a candidate with a disability, or are assisting a candidate with a disability, and require an accommodation to apply for one of our jobs, please email us at GMWTalentOperations@wellington.com.

Benefits

At Wellington Management, our approach to compensation is designed to help us attract, inspire and retain the best talent in our industry. We strive to pay employees fairly and competitively across all levels and roles. Our approach to compensation considers all aspects of total compensation; all employees are eligible to receive salary, variable compensation, and benefits. The base salary range for this position is:

USD 90,000 - 180,000

This range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered when making compensation decisions, including but not limited to skill sets; role; skills and experience; certifications; and education. This range is an estimate, and further details on salary and total compensation aspects will be shared with candidates during the recruitment process.

Base salary is only one component of Wellington’s total compensation approach. Other rewards may include a discretionary Corporate Bonus and/ or Incentives, if eligible. In addition, we offer a comprehensive and high value benefit package to meet the unique needs of our employees and their families, and we are committed to fostering a flexible work environment that enables employees to thrive personally and professionally. Examples of our benefits include retirement plan, health and wellbeing, dental, vision, and pharmacy coverage, health savings account, flexible spending accounts and commuter program, employee assistance program, life and disability insurance, adoption assistance, back-up childcare, tuition/CFA reimbursement and paid time off (leave of absence, paid holidays, volunteer, sick and vacation time)

We believe that in person interactions inspire and energize our community and are essential to our culture. In support of this commitment, our employees work from our offices 4 days a week with flexibility to work remotely 1 day a week. We believe that this approach ultimately supports our mission to deliver investment excellence to our clients and their beneficiaries over the long term.

Title: Data & Product Analyst (Benchmarking), CoStar Debt Solutions
Description:
Job Description

Data & Product Analyst (Benchmarking)

Location: Boston, in-office

About The Role

CoStar Debt Solutions is building the next generation of CRE analytics software — a platform where data, benchmarking intelligence, and client workflows come together in a single experience to support how lenders originate, evaluate, and manage risk.

A central part of this vision is our Benchmarking product, which enables lenders to compare loan performance, pricing, and risk characteristics against a trusted market dataset. This product is rapidly evolving, with significant investment in expanding coverage, improving methodologies, and delivering more actionable insights directly into client workflows.

We’re hiring a Data & Product Analyst to help drive the continued growth of this Benchmarking product — both as a data asset and as a highly client-facing solution.

This role combines data analysis, product development, and direct client engagement, with a strong emphasis on supporting client adoption and enabling the sales process. You will work closely with clients and internal sales teams to demonstrate product value, answer analytical questions, and ensure clients can effectively leverage benchmarking insights in their workflows.

In year one, this role will focus on analyzing benchmark data, supporting product enhancements, and actively participating in client meetings, product demos, and sales support activities. Over time, the role expands into shaping benchmark methodologies, influencing product strategy, and helping scale how benchmarking insights are delivered across the platform.

This is a hybrid role at the intersection of data analysis, product development, and client/sales engagement — ideal for someone who can translate complex datasets into clear insights and communicate them effectively to both internal and external audiences.

What You’ll Own


The analysis of complex datasets that power the Benchmarking product — identifying trends, inconsistencies, and opportunities to improve data coverage and quality
The evolution of benchmark methodologies, outputs, and usability in partnership with Product Managers and cross-functional teams
Direct engagement with clients, including leading and supporting client conversations to understand benchmarking use cases, answer analytical questions, and gather actionable feedback
Active support of sales and go-to-market efforts, including participating in product demonstrations, responding to client inquiries, and helping articulate the value of benchmarking insights
Ongoing client support and enablement, ensuring users can interpret and apply benchmark data effectively in their workflows
Collaboration with engineering teams to ensure accurate delivery of benchmark data, calculations, and features
Monitoring product usage and client feedback to identify areas for improvement and drive continuous enhancements
Data validation, quality checks, and troubleshooting to maintain the reliability and integrity of benchmark datasets
Staying current on industry trends and competitive benchmarking solutions to inform product direction


What We Expect You To Bring


Bachelor’s degree from an accredited, not-for-profit, in person, university or college. Ideally in Data Analytics, Data Science, Business Analytics, Finance, Economics, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field
2+ years of experience working with data analytics, financial data, or data-driven products
Strong hands-on experience working with large datasets and performing detailed analysis
Strong communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with both technical stakeholders and clients
Proven ability to support client-facing interactions, including presenting, explaining analytical concepts, and responding to client questions in real time
Experience with analytics or benchmarking products, or similar data-driven solutions
Strong analytical thinking, attention to detail, and problem-solving skills
A track record of commitment to prior employers


Nice To Have


Exposure to SQL, Python, or similar languages
Experience with benchmarking, peer comparison, or performance analytics solutions
Experience supporting client-facing products or working in a customer-oriented environment
Familiarity with financial services, lending, or real estate data
Experience with data visualization tools
Understanding of APIs and data integration concepts


The Growth Path

The first year in this role is focused on deeply understanding the benchmark dataset, client needs, and current product capabilities — contributing directly to data analysis, active client engagement, sales support, and incremental product improvements. You will play a key role in client conversations, product demonstrations, and helping drive adoption of benchmarking insights in real-world workflows.

Beyond that, the role expands into a more strategic position:


Shaping how benchmark methodologies evolve as the dataset scales
Driving enhancements to how insights are surfaced within client workflows
Partnering with sales and client teams to improve how benchmarking is positioned, adopted, and delivered
Influencing product direction based on client usage patterns, feedback, and market trends


This role is a strong path into broader product ownership, client-facing product strategy, or advanced analytics leadership, particularly for someone interested in building and scaling data-driven products that directly support client outcomes and business growth.

What’s Unique About This Role

Most data analyst roles focus on generating insights. This role goes further — connecting those insights directly to product decisions and client outcomes.

You’ll Not Only Analyze Data, But Also


Work directly with clients and sales teams to translate insights into adoption and business value
Play a key role in client-facing discussions that shape both product direction and commercial success
Help bridge the gap between data, product, and revenue-generating activities


What’s in it for you?

When you join CoStar Group, you’ll experience a collaborative and innovative culture working alongside the best and brightest to empower our people and customers to succeed. We offer you generous compensation and performance-based incentives. CoStar Group also invests in your professional and academic growth with internal training, and tuition reimbursement.

Our Benefits Package Includes (but Is Not Limited To)


Comprehensive healthcare coverage: Medical / Vision / Dental / Prescription Drug
Life, legal, and supplementary insurance
Virtual and in person mental health counseling services for individuals and family
Commuter and parking benefits
401(K) retirement plan with matching contributions
Employee stock purchase plan
Paid time off
Tuition reimbursement
On-site fitness center and/or reimbursed fitness center membership costs (location dependent)
Access to CoStar Group’s Employee Resource Groups
Complimentary gourmet coffee, tea, hot chocolate, fresh fruit, and other healthy snacks


This position offers an annual base salary range of $99,000 - $133,000, based on relevant skills and experience and includes a generous benefits plan

We welcome all qualified candidates who are currently eligible to work full-time in the United States to apply. However, please note that CoStar Group is not able to provide visa sponsorship for this position.

CoStar Group is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer; we maintain a drug-free workplace and perform pre-employment substance abuse testing

This position is an anticipated vacancy. It is expected to be vacant by 08/16/2026. However, the current incumbent has a right to rescind their retirement, leave, or resignation up until the day of the expected vacancy date. Your hire will not be confirmed until the position is vacated, and you may start the year as a Long-Term Substitute if the position does not become vacant by the start of the school year.

REPORTS TO: Director of Organizational Insight

Position Overview

The Data Analyst for Strategic Initiatives resides in the Office of Data and Accountability (ODA) in the Division of Data, Information and Systems Improvement in Boston Public Schools. The Data Analyst leads complex analytical projects that inform district policy, strategic decision-making, and operational implementation. This role is responsible for designing and executing sophisticated analyses, managing data for high-impact district initiatives, and ensuring the integrity and accessibility of district data.

The Data Analyst serves as a technical expert in educational data, statistical analysis, and data visualization, translating complex information into actionable insights for district leadership, schools, and the community. The position requires advanced analytical expertise, exceptional project management skills, and the ability to collaborate across departments to deliver accurate, timely, and meaningful data products.

As a member of a highly collaborative team, the Data Analyst contributes to enterprise-wide data initiatives, supports the development of district data analyses and dashboards, and provides mentorship and technical leadership on complex analytical projects.

Responsibilities

Strategic Data Analysis and Policy Support


Lead complex district analyses that support strategic initiatives, policy implementation, and executive decision-making.
Design and conduct statistical analyses using student-, school-, and district-level data to identify trends, evaluate outcomes, and inform continuous improvement.
Develop recurring and ad hoc analyses and/or dashboards for district leadership, School Committee presentations, and public reporting.
Translate technical findings into clear reports, visualizations, and recommendations for both technical and non-technical audiences.
Provide technical consultation to district departments, schools, and external stakeholders regarding data collection, interpretation, and analysis.


Exam School Admissions Analytics


Lead the annual analytical processes supporting the district's exam school admissions policy.
Develop and validate socioeconomic tier calculations using census and geographic data in accordance with School Committee policy.
Manage the collection, standardization, validation, and calculation of student GPAs across BPS and non-BPS schools.
Conduct multiple rounds of quality assurance and validation to ensure accuracy and integrity of admissions calculations.
Produce annual reporting and supporting analyses for School Committee presentations and public communications.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure accurate and timely implementation of the admissions process and governance of data elements related to selective admissions.


Project Management and Cross-Functional Collaboration


Manage multiple complex analytical projects simultaneously while meeting competing deadlines.
Coordinate work across departments to ensure successful implementation of district initiatives.
Facilitate meetings with stakeholders to gather requirements, review findings, prioritize work, and resolve issues.
Represent the Office of Data and Accountability on district committees, project teams, and cross-functional initiatives.
Collaborate with district departments and technical teams within ODA to define business requirements, establish shared reporting standards, and maintain consistent data definitions.
Support data governance initiatives by promoting best practices for reporting, data quality, and documentation.
Fulfill data requests from internal and external members of the BPS community by extracting data from internal databases, including ad-hoc and recurring requests
Support student privacy regulations as mandated by FERPA, HIPAA, IDEA, MA DESE, City of Boston, and BPS; facilitate the execution of data sharing agreements where applicable
Provide technical assistance to school and central staff regarding data needs, assessments, and analyses.
Perform other relevant duties in the Office of Data and Accountability as needed


Qualifications – Required


Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Data Analytics, Education Research, Computer Science, Public Policy, or a related field.
Minimum of three years of experience analyzing complex K–12 education data.
Demonstrated experience managing high-profile analytical projects involving multiple stakeholders.
Advanced proficiency in SQL and at least one statistical programming language (R, Python, or Stata).
Experience developing interactive dashboards using Power BI or comparable business intelligence platforms.
Experience working with relational databases and large-scale datasets.
Strong understanding of statistical methods, data validation, quality assurance, and analytic best practices.
Excellent project management, organizational, and prioritization skills.
Demonstrated ability to explain complex analytical concepts to diverse audiences.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to collaborate effectively across technical and non-technical teams.
Commitment to educational equity and using data to improve outcomes for students.
Authorization to work in the United States.


Qualifications – Preferred


Master's degree in Data Analytics, Statistics, Education Research, Public Policy, Computer Science, or related field.
Experience supporting district-wide policy implementation or accountability systems.
Knowledge of census, geographic, or demographic data analysis.
Experience with data governance, enterprise reporting, or business intelligence strategy.
Familiarity with Boston Public Schools or another large urban school district.

Description:
Position: Technical Data Analyst

Location: Boston, MA (Hybrid)

Duration: Multi Year Renewable Contract

Hours: 37.5 Hours per week

Rate: $60-65/hr W2

Overview

We are seeking a highly analytical and detail-oriented Technical Data Analyst to support enterprise data quality, migration, and integration initiatives. The ideal candidate will have experience assessing, profiling, cleansing, validating, and transforming large datasets while developing reporting and integration solutions to support business and technical teams.

Required Qualifications


Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Analytics, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
5+ years of experience in data analysis, data quality, or data management within enterprise environments.
Strong understanding of data governance, data quality principles, and data lifecycle management.


Technical Skills


Experience performing data profiling to assess completeness, accuracy, consistency, uniqueness, and validity of enterprise data.
Proven ability to execute data cleansing, standardization, deduplication, and validation activities using established data quality methodologies.
Experience developing and maintaining data mapping documents, data conversion templates, validation templates, reconciliation reports, and data quality scorecards.
Proficiency in writing SQL and scripting (e.g., Python, PowerShell, or similar) to automate data cleansing, transformation, validation, and reconciliation processes.
Experience creating automated validation routines to compare source and target datasets and identify data quality issues.
Strong knowledge of relational databases and data modeling concepts.


Reporting & Analytics


Experience developing interactive dashboards and reports using Tableau and/or Microsoft Power BI.
Ability to analyze data quality metrics and communicate findings through executive dashboards and technical reports.
Experience creating KPIs and visualizations to monitor data quality, migration progress, and operational performance.


Integration & APIs


Experience working with MuleSoft for API-led integrations and enterprise data exchange.
Understanding of RESTful APIs, JSON, XML, and enterprise integration patterns.
Experience supporting API testing, validation, and troubleshooting.
Familiarity with integrating cloud applications, including CRM platforms such as Salesforce, using APIs.


Preferred Qualifications


Experience supporting Salesforce CRM implementations, migrations, or data quality initiatives.
Experience with ETL/data integration tools and enterprise data migration projects.
Familiarity with data quality platforms such as Cloudingo, DemandTools, Informatica, Talend, or similar solutions.
Experience working in Agile delivery environments.
Knowledge of healthcare, provider, payer, or regulated industry data is preferred.


Key Responsibilities


Perform data profiling and quality assessments to identify gaps, inconsistencies, duplicates, and validation issues.
Design and execute data cleansing and transformation activities to improve data quality.
Develop scripts and automated processes for data validation, cleansing, reconciliation, and exception reporting.
Create and maintain data mapping documents, conversion templates, and validation artifacts.
Build Tableau and Power BI dashboards to monitor data quality, migration readiness, and business metrics.
Support API integrations and data exchange using MuleSoft and REST APIs.

Roux is seeking a Database Analyst with hands-on experience using EarthSoft’s EQuIS to support the management of environmental and chemical data for analysis and reporting. The ideal candidate is an experienced analyst with a desire to grow who can execute day-to-day EDD processing and project support while also supporting EQuIS database administration, configuration, and client-facing dashboard/reporting capabilities. Candidate is expected to work from the Burlington, Massachusetts office three days per week at minimum.

Position Requirements


Bachelor’s degree or higher in relevant technical field.
Minimum of 4 years of environmental data management experience, including practical use of EarthSoft’s EQuIS in a consulting or regulated environment.
Demonstrated experience processing and QA/QC’ing laboratory EDDs efficiently using EQuIS (EDP) (or comparable EDD workflow).
Working knowledge of EQuIS configuration/administration concepts.
Strong skills and proficiency with Microsoft-based software, including MS Access and MS Excel.
Interest and aptitude for building client-facing outputs (dashboards/reporting) using EQuIS dashboards.
Basic to intermediate SQL skills for querying, troubleshooting, and supporting reports/dashboards.
Strong attention to detail and problem-solving capabilities.
Ability to manage multiple project priorities and tight schedules.
Strong written and verbal communication skills for coordination with project managers, laboratories, and technical staff.
Ability to help build and scale Roux’s EQuIS capabilities by training and supporting other staff, including analysts with prior database experience.

Support environmental project teams by managing, processing, and quality‑checking environmental data in EQuIS to ensure datasets are accurate, complete, and suitable for reporting, compliance, and analysis.
Collaborate closely with project managers, scientists, engineers, and GIS staff to understand project requirements, prioritize data tasks, and deliver high‑quality data support under tight timelines.
Process laboratory and field EDDs in EQuIS (EDP), perform QA/QC and completeness checks, resolve common errors efficiently, and coordinate corrections with labs and project staff.
Support routine data tracking, data loading, and data delivery workflows.

Title: Analyst, Data Governance
Description:
About Us

National Grid is hiring an Analyst for our Data Governance department in Upstate, NY / Downstate, NY or Waltham, NE.

Everyday we deliver safe and secure energy to homes, communities, and businesses. We are there when people need us the most. We connect people to the energy they need for the lives they live. The pace of change in society and our industry is accelerating and our expertise and track record puts us in an unparalleled position to shape the sustainable future of our industry.

To be successful we must anticipate the needs of our customers, reducing the cost of energy delivery today and pioneering the flexible energy systems of tomorrow. This requires us to deliver on our promises and always look for new opportunities to grow, both ourselves and our business

Job Purpose

The position reports to the Manager, Data Governance. The Data Governance Analyst functions as a partner for the Data team working closely with IT, business, product and platform teams. The Data Governance Analyst will bring the capability of defining and maintaining new processes inclusive of end to end data requirements. Title: Competitive Intelligence Research
Description:
As a Senior Analyst in Meta’s Competitive Intelligence organization, you will operate at the intersection of advanced analytics, data science, and market strategy. You will lead major projects and product areas—often in environments of significant ambiguity or technical complexity—driving both technical and business outcomes. This is a hands-on, high-impact role for builders who thrive on solving real problems. This role demands a unique blend of analytical and statistical expertise, strategic thinking , and the ability to translate complex insights into impactful product and business decisions. You will be recognized as a thought partner by cross-functional leads and will help shape the analytical foundations that inform how we build and grow our products.

Competitive Intelligence Research Responsibilities:


Market Strategy: Influence organization-level product direction through data-driven narratives and an in depth understanding of the market landscape. Demonstrated experience operating at scale, and across ambiguous, environments with working knowledge of econometrics. As a quantitative market-strategist, you will blend practical and applied understanding with technical expertise, including pressure-testing data for quality, reliability, understanding data-biases and being solution driven
Analytics Leadership: Conduct advanced analyses with 3P datasets, develop statistical models and forecasts, and deliver actionable insights that informs market and business strategy. These include, but are not limited to:
Data onboarding: Identify, onboard, and rigorously evaluate 3P datasets to determine their signal-to-noise ratio and predictive power
Data triangulation: Triangulate data from many sources of imperfect information. Synthesize multiple, low-fidelity 3rd-party signals into a single high-fidelity trend report using Bayesian aggregation or other methods
Data transformation: Apply quasi-experimental designs (e.g., synthetic control, diff-in-diff) to isolate the impact of exogenous market shocks and competitor actions on internal performance metrics, using 3rd-party behavioral and economic datasets
Insight and implications: Apply guidance from such analyses to increase the accuracy of forecasts and better understand market trends
Technical & Methodological Expertise: Act as a recognized professional in a technical or methodological area (e.g., causal inference, bayesian aggregation), driving the adoption of advanced methods and organization-wide best practices that raise the bar for the entire team
Data Governance & Quality: Ensure data privacy, security, and compliance with organizational standards. Champion data quality frameworks and documentation practices that enable credible reproducible analyses
Resourceful, adaptable professional with a bias for action


Minimum Qualifications:


Bachelors degree and a minimum of 6 years of work experience (minimum of 4 years with a Ph.D.) in business intelligence, product analytics, or economic or strategy consulting in a technology environment with increasing scope and impact
Demonstrated skill to ethically source, validate, and synthesize high-signal insights from people (e.g., stakeholder interviews, skilled conversations, field research, and relationship-based information gathering) while maintaining high standards for privacy, consent, and integrity
Proficiency in AI-powered tools: Demonstrate working knowledge of Generative AI technologies (e.g., LLM and AI agents) and experience designing, prompting, and orchestrating AI systems (e.g., prompt engineering) to automate data analyses, synthesize insights, and execute multi-step analytical tasks (e.g., prompting agent to clean datasets, build visualizations)
Practical working understanding of data-analytics tools, and direct experience managing, analyzing, manipulating and interpreting 1P and external 3P datasets
Experience with data querying languages (e.g., SQL), scripting languages (e.g., Python), and/or statistical/mathematical software (e.g., R)
Proven experience with statistical analysis including causal inference (e.g., randomized control trials, quasi-experimentation such as synthetic control, diff-in-diff, meta-analyses), and/or bayesian aggregation (e.g., bayesian pooling, hierarchical modeling)
Demonstrated communication skills and experience presenting complex findings to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Demonstrated experience thriving in ambiguous environments and shape new analytics organizations or products


Preferred Qualifications:


Master's or Ph.D. Degree in a quantitative field such as Quantitative Economics or Political Science, Operations Research, Data Science, Computer Science, Physics, Business, or Mathematics
Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies


About Meta:

Meta builds technologies that help people connect, find communities, and grow businesses. When Facebook launched in 2004, it changed the way people connect. Apps like Messenger, Instagram and WhatsApp further empowered billions around the world. Now, Meta is moving beyond 2D screens toward immersive experiences like augmented and virtual reality to help build the next evolution in social technology. People who choose to build their careers by building with us at Meta help shape a future that will take us beyond what digital connection makes possible today—beyond the constraints of screens, the limits of distance, and even the rules of physics.

Meta is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Meta participates in the E-Verify program in certain locations, as required by law. Please note that Meta may leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies in connection with applications for employment.

Meta is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities in our recruiting process. If you need any assistance or accommodations due to a disability, please let us know at accommodations-ext@meta.com.

Individual compensation is determined by skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Compensation details listed in this posting reflect the base hourly rate, monthly rate, or annual salary only, and do not include bonus, equity or sales incentives, if applicable. Title: Research Analyst-Department of research and planning
Description:
Official Title: Research Analyst

Pay Grade: Grade 22S

Salary Range: 22S Entry Level Pay $92,999.66 to Pay Range Maximum $137,066.54

Starting Pay: $92,999.66/yr.

Salary Notes: This position is designated as a Union position. All new hires must start at the entry level rate for this role per the collective bargaining agreement/MOA with OPEIU, Local 6. Pay may advance within the salary band according to the CBA/MOU.

Departmental Mission Statement: The mission of the Department of Research and Planning is to support research in the Trial Court; to assist court staff in using empirical research to improve court operations; and to promote the use of research to inform and further improve the justice system.

Organizational Profile

https://www.mass.gov/orgs/trial-court-department-of-research-and-planning

Notes


This position is fully on site Monday-Friday.


Position Summary: Conducts high-level quantitative and qualitative analysis to assist in Trial Court planning and decision-making. Designs, creates, and manages data systems to support dashboards, tables, charts, figures, and reports to display information in a simple usable manner. Analyzes data to draw conclusions and make recommendations of operation. Provides support to end users of research products.

Supervision Received: Works under the direction of the Department Head.

Essential Functions And Responsibilities


Conducts analysis of case processing and other topics as assigned.
Extracts reports and explains coherent narratives from vast amounts of data concerning bail decisions, default rates, civil party representation, etc.
Creates Tableau dashboards for Trial Court leadership and the public.
Creates reports, charts, tables and graphics for Trial Court leadership and the public.
Conducts research projects as directed by the Director of Research and Planning, including projects at the request of Trial Court leadership, required by statute, or requested by an external stakeholder.
Maintains and updates monthly, quarterly, and annual dashboards for various Trial Court departments and offices.
Provides administrative support to the Massachusetts Sentencing Commission.
Assists with and/or conducts research projects as assigned by the Director of Research and Planning.
Performs other duties as required.


Job Competencies: Ethics and Values: Communicates and demonstrates the ethics and values of the Trial Court.

Mission Driven: Employees are fully committed to fulfilling the Trial Court and associated Departmental missions.

Professional Development: Employees are committed to participating in ongoing Trial Court training and educational offerings to advance their professional development. Managers are equally committed to affording opportunities to those they supervise as scheduling permits.

Customer Service: Conducts oneself in a courteous and professional manner towards both Trial Court employees and the public.

Applied Knowledge: Ability to communicate and present data and research findings such as graphs, tables, and technical briefs.

Problem Solving: Ability to successfully address research issues, draw conclusions and make recommendations based on the research and policy analysis results.

Commitment to Diversity: Promotes an environment of diversity through understanding, respect, and positive communication with persons of varied racial, ethnic, economic, and cultural backgrounds.

Collaboration: Works with others cooperatively, and promotes teamwork, contributing to a work environment that focuses on shared departmental goals.

Minimum Requirements: Education and Experience:


Bachelor's Degree from an accredited college or university; Graduate degree preferred
Three (3) years of related work experience
Equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered for meeting minimum qualifications.


Knowledge, Skills and Abilities: Knowledge of:


Trial Court business and practices.
Advisory Sentencing Guidelines.
MassCourts and DataMart.
Department operations and subject matter.
Research methodology.
Various applicable software programs, including Tableau, Excel, and other business intelligence software.
Database management and Extract Transfer and Load (ETL) tools.
Dashboard design.
Courtyard web posting.


Skill In


Data research and analysis.
Survey evaluation.
Verbal and written communication.
Organization and prioritization.


Ability To


Respond to requests.
Conduct literature reviews.
Utilize database warehouses.
Create, maintain, and edit documents.
Correspond and collaborate with various stakeholders.
Maintain productive working relationships with others.


Supervisory Responsibility: This position serves as a lead worker to others, including third-party contractors.

Working Conditions: Work is frequently performed in office or similar indoor environments.

Physical Demands: This position requires sedentary work:

Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally, a negligible amount of force frequently, and/or constantly having to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects, including the human body. Sedentary work involves sitting most of the time. Jobs are sedentary if walking and standing are required only occasionally and all other sedentary criteria are met.

Title: Rotational Undergraduate Analyst - MSI
Description:
Why MSI? We thrive on solving challenges.

As a leading MGA, MSI combines deep underwriting expertise with insurer risk capacity to create specialized insurance solutions that empower distribution partners to meet customers’ unique needs.

We have a passion for crafting solutions for the important risks facing individuals and businesses. We offer an expanding suite of products – from fully-digital embedded renters coverage to high-value homeowners insurance to sophisticated commercial coverages, such as cyber liability and habitational property – delivered through agents, brokers, wholesalers and other brand partners.

Our partners and customers count on us to deliver exceptional service through a dedicated team that makes rapid resolutions a priority. We simplify the insurance experience through our advanced technology platform that supports every phase of the policy lifecycle. Bring on your challenges and let us show you how we build insurance better.

The Rotational Undergraduate Analyst Program is a distinguished early-career opportunity designed for high-potential undergraduate students seeking to explore multiple facets of our organization. Spanning from Claims, Underwriting and Product, this immersive rotational program provides hands-on experience, training, professional development, and intensive mentorship, preparing participants to become well-rounded analysts and future leaders. At the end of the program, you will have the opportunity to join one of the teams you work with.

Program Overview

Participants in the Rotational Undergraduate Analyst Program will embark on a journey that typically spans [18–24] months, divided into 12 months in Product, 6 months in Claims, and 6 months in Underwriting for both Personal and Commercial Lines. Throughout the program, analysts will be exposed to a variety of business challenges, contribute to high-impact projects, and engage with colleagues from diverse backgrounds and expertise.


Duration: 24 months
Departments: Product, Underwriting, Claims
Location: Boston, MA (hybrid, three days in office)
Start Date: August 2027


Key Responsibilities

As a Rotational Undergraduate Analyst, you will:


Participate in multiple assignments across different business units to gain comprehensive organizational insight
Analyze qualitative and quantitative data to support strategic decision-making
Contribute to cross-functional teams on high-impact projects and initiatives
Develop and deliver presentations on findings and recommendations to business leaders
Assist with process improvement, operational optimization, and digital transformation efforts
Conduct market research and competitive benchmarking
Collaborate with mentors, managers, and fellow analysts to enhance learning and performance
Document and share knowledge gained from each rotation to inform future assignments
Engage in structured training, workshops, and networking events
Demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a commitment to continuous growth


Qualifications

Required:


Bachelor’s degree in Risk Management, Business, Economics, Data Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Liberal Arts or a related field
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills
Excellent written and verbal communication abilities
Demonstrated leadership potential through academics, extracurricular activities, internships, or volunteer work
Ability to work collaboratively in diverse teams and adapt to new situations quickly
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word); familiarity with data analysis tools (e.g., SQL, Tableau, Python) is a plus
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
Authorized to work in the country of employment without sponsorship


Preferred


Previous internship or work experience in a related field
Coursework or projects involving data analysis, business strategy, or technology
Interest in pursuing a long-term career with our organization
Multilingual abilities and/or international experience


Professional Development & Mentorship

The Rotational Undergraduate Analyst Program offers comprehensive training, access to leadership development resources, and ongoing mentorship from experienced professionals. Each analyst is paired with both a rotation supervisor and a program mentor, ensuring personalized guidance and support throughout the program.

Participants will attend workshops and seminars covering topics such as:


Business acumen and industry trends, and professional designations such as, but not limited to CPCU, AINS, Are, ARM
Technical skills (data analytics, project management, presentation skills)
Professional networking and personal branding
Leadership and team dynamics
Career planning and goal setting
Networking events and leadership panels with company executives, program alumni, and subject matter experts provide valuable opportunities for career exploration and relationship building.


Performance Evaluation & Feedback

Analysts receive ongoing feedback from rotation supervisors and participate in formal performance reviews at the end of each rotation. Evaluations focus on technical proficiency, business impact, collaboration, adaptability, and leadership potential. Individual development plans are designed to address growth areas and capitalize on strengths, ensuring continual progress throughout the program.

Starting pay is $65,000+, negotiable at time of offer.

The Rotational Undergraduate Analyst Program is a distinguished early-career opportunity designed for high-potential undergraduate students seeking to explore multiple facets of our organization. Spanning from Claims, Underwriting and Product, this immersive rotational program provides hands-on experience, training, professional development, and intensive mentorship, preparing participants to become well-rounded analysts and future leaders. At the end of the program, you will have the opportunity to join one of the teams you work with.

Program Overview

Participants in the Rotational Undergraduate Analyst Program will embark on a journey that typically spans [18–24] months, divided into 12 months in Product, 6 months in Claims, and 6 months in Underwriting for both Personal and Commercial Lines. Throughout the program, analysts will be exposed to a variety of business challenges, contribute to high-impact projects, and engage with colleagues from diverse backgrounds and expertise.

  • Duration: 24 months
  • Departments: Product, Underwriting, Claims
  • Location: Boston, MA (hybrid, three days in office)
  • Start Date: August 2027

Key Responsibilities

As a Rotational Undergraduate Analyst, you will:

  • Participate in multiple assignments across different business units to gain comprehensive organizational insight
  • Analyze qualitative and quantitative data to support strategic decision-making
  • Contribute to cross-functional teams on high-impact projects and initiatives
  • Develop and deliver presentations on findings and recommendations to business leaders
  • Assist with process improvement, operational optimization, and digital transformation efforts
  • Conduct market research and competitive benchmarking
  • Collaborate with mentors, managers, and fellow analysts to enhance learning and performance
  • Document and share knowledge gained from each rotation to inform future assignments
  • Engage in structured training, workshops, and networking events
  • Demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a commitment to continuous growth

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Risk Management, Business, Economics, Data Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Liberal Arts or a related field
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills
  • Excellent written and verbal communication abilities
  • Demonstrated leadership potential through academics, extracurricular activities, internships, or volunteer work
  • Ability to work collaboratively in diverse teams and adapt to new situations quickly
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word); familiarity with data analysis tools (e.g., SQL, Tableau, Python) is a plus
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
  • Authorized to work in the country of employment without sponsorship

Preferred

  • Previous internship or work experience in a related field
  • Coursework or projects involving data analysis, business strategy, or technology
  • Interest in pursuing a long-term career with our organization
  • Multilingual abilities and/or international experience

Professional Development & Mentorship

The Rotational Undergraduate Analyst Program offers comprehensive training, access to leadership development resources, and ongoing mentorship from experienced professionals. Each analyst is paired with both a rotation supervisor and a program mentor, ensuring personalized guidance and support throughout the program.

Participants will attend workshops and seminars covering topics such as:

  • Business acumen and industry trends, and professional designations such as, but not limited to CPCU, AINS, Are, ARM
  • Technical skills (data analytics, project management, presentation skills)
  • Professional networking and personal branding
  • Leadership and team dynamics
  • Career planning and goal setting
  • Networking events and leadership panels with company executives, program alumni, and subject matter experts provide valuable opportunities for career exploration and relationship building.

Performance Evaluation & Feedback

Analysts receive ongoing feedback from rotation supervisors and participate in formal performance reviews at the end of each rotation. Evaluations focus on technical proficiency, business impact, collaboration, adaptability, and leadership potential. Individual development plans are designed to address growth areas and capitalize on strengths, ensuring continual progress throughout the program.

Starting pay is $65,000+, negotiable at time of offer.

Title: Product Analyst
Description:
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock human performance and healthspan. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives.

WHOOP is hiring Product Analysts to embed across the product organization and serve as strategic analytics partners to teams across Healthcare, Algorithms, AI, Hardware, and other product areas. In this role, you will help define how WHOOP measures product success, uncover insights that shape roadmap decisions, and translate complex data into clear recommendations that improve the member experience. You will bring strong analytical rigor, product intuition, and intellectual curiosity to help teams make faster, smarter, and more impactful decisions with data.

Responsibilities


Partner with Product, Engineering, Research, Design, and cross-functional leadership to inform strategy and roadmap decisions with data.
Own the analytical narrative for your product area, illustrated by defining KPIs, refining measurement frameworks, and surfacing insights that drive action.
Support experimentation and feature launches end-to-end: from defining success metrics to post-launch analysis and iteration.
Build scalable, self-serve reporting & tooling that lets your stakeholders make decisions without waiting on you.
Develop deep context on your product domain and use it to ask sharper questions, challenge assumptions, and push the product forward.
Proactively surface insights and recommendations that go beyond the ask; identify opportunities others haven't seen yet.
Collaborate with a high-performance analytics team in a fast-paced environment where intellectual curiosity is the baseline expectation.


Qualifications


You've done this before: 2-6+ years in an analytical role where you owned business-critical metrics or initiatives. (We're hiring across levels; we'll figure out the right fit together.)
You use AI tools proactively and hold AI-assisted work to the same bar as your own.
You can take a vague question, wrangle the right data, isolate insights, and communicate actionable recommendations to stakeholders who aren't data people.
You're a strong storyteller: you know how to make a compelling, concise case for action.
You're technically sharp: advanced SQL is table stakes. Familiarity with modern data stacks (Snowflake, dbt, ELT workflows) and visualization tools (Hex, Sigma, Amplitude, Looker) is a plus.
You have product sense: you think about the member experience, not just the numbers.
You're curious about how things work. Algorithms, hardware, health science: you don't need to be an expert, but you should want to understand.
You're a self-starter who thrives in ambiguity and doesn't wait to be told what to work on.
TEAMS WE'RE HIRING FOR


We’re Looking For Multiple Analysts To Work Across Our Product Teams. During The Interview Process, We'll Work With You To Find The Right Team Fit Based On Your Interests And Strengths


AI Product: The future of intelligent coaching and personalized insights powered by AI/ML.
Algorithms: Where the science meets the product; sleep, recovery, strain, and how algorithmic outputs translate into member value.
Hardware Product: The physical device experience; sensors, wearability, and next-gen hardware.
Healthcare Product: Building WHOOP's Health Operating System; health outcomes, clinical features, personalized wellness.


This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office.

Interested in the role, but don’t meet every qualification? We encourage you to still apply! At WHOOP, we believe there is much more to a candidate than what is written on paper, and we value character as much as experience. As we continue to build a diverse and inclusive environment, we encourage anyone who is interested in this role to apply.

WHOOP is an Equal Opportunity Employer and participates in E-verify to determine employment eligibility

The WHOOP compensation philosophy is designed to attract, motivate, and retain exceptional talent by offering competitive base salaries, meaningful equity, and consistent pay practices that reflect our mission and core values.

At WHOOP, we view total compensation as the combination of base salary, equity, and benefits, with equity serving as a key differentiator that aligns our employees with the long-term success of the company and allows every member of our corporate team to own part of WHOOP and share in the company’s long-term growth and success.

The U.S. base salary range for this full-time position is $100,000 - $155,000. Salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within each range, individual pay is based on factors such as job-related skills, experience, performance, and relevant education or training.

In addition to the base salary, the successful candidate will also receive benefits and a generous equity package.

These ranges may be modified in the future to reflect evolving market conditions and organizational needs. While most offers will typically fall toward the starting point of the range, total compensation will depend on the candidate’s specific qualifications, expertise, and alignment with the role’s requirements.

Title: Lead Data Analyst (Network)
Description:
About Agero:Wherever drivers go, we’re leading the way. Agero’s mission is to rethink the vehicle ownership experience through a powerful combination of passionate people and data-driven technology, strengthening our clients’ relationships with their customers. As the #1 B2B, white-label provider of digital driver assistance services, we’re pushing the industry in a new direction, taking manual processes, and redefining them as digital, transparent, and connected. This includes: an industry-leading dispatch management platform powered by Swoop; comprehensive accident management services; knowledgeable consumer affairs and connected vehicle capabilities; and a growing marketplace of services, discounts and support enabled by a robust partner ecosystem. The company has over 150 million vehicle coverage points in partnership with leading automobile manufacturers, insurance carriers and many others. Managing one of the largest national networks of service providers, Agero responds to approximately 12 million service events annually. Agero, a member company of The Cross Country Group, is headquartered in Medford, Mass., with operations throughout North America. To learn more, visit https://www.agero.com/.

Note: For our technical positions, we love to get you started in person! You may be required to travel to Medford for your initial onboarding. Don't worry about the logistics - once you're hired, we handle all travel arrangements and expenses for you.

Position Summary

The Lead Data Analyst (Network) is at the forefront of data-driven initiatives for the group, acting as a linchpin between raw data and actionable insights. This position dissects complex datasets, identifies  patterns, and leverages those insights to drive business growth. Collaborates closely with various internal and external stakeholders, helping them understand the data and how this information can shape future strategies.

Responsibilities:

Advanced Analytics: Develop and deploy advanced analytical models to improve our understanding of Network supply and demand, identify operational inefficiencies, and deliver actionable recommendations to leadership
Performance Monitoring: Implement real-time dashboards and reporting to track and assess Network performance against established metrics
Network Strategy Innovation: Challenge the status quo and be willing to propose and test new strategies for increasing competition and engagement within our service provider network
Stakeholder Feedback Analysis: Analyze feedback, ratings, and reviews from multiple sources and stakeholders to gain insights into service quality, customer satisfaction, and provider satisfaction, identifying actionable insights for improvement
Service Provider Insights: Develop operational and performance data to generate actionable insights and recommendations for 3rd party service providers, enabling them to enhance their service delivery, optimize processes, and align more closely with organizational objectives
Capacity Analysis and Modeling: Analyze the capacity of our Network, identifying gaps, weaknesses, and opportunities to improve operational efficiency and service quality, making recommendations for Network recruiting, retention, and optimization
Testing: Leads test and pilots for process changes as a a result of analysis and communicates the results and recommendations to all areas of management
Subject matter expert: Serves as an internal data analytics expert by ensuring consistency in data analysis methodologies and sharing of best practices

Experience and Skills:

BA/BS Degree or equivalent experience. Degree that emphasizes data analysis and communication (e.g., computer science, social sciences, physical sciences, math, engineering, or statistics) preferred
5+ years of business and data analysis experience
Excellent communication and presentation abilities
Strong problem-solving skills and business acumen
Experience with data management, specifically with validating and auditing data and reports from multiple systems
Demonstrated project and task management capability
Past experience with BI, Google Workspace, and CRM Tools
Proficiency in SQL and working with relational databases is required
An analytical professional with attention to detail and high standard of performance excellence

Hiring In:

United States: Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Massachusetts, Michigan, New Hampshire, New York State, New Mexico, North Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia

The anticipated closing date to submit applications for this role is June 20th, 2026. Join our Greenhouse Candidate Portal to track your application status and receive instant alerts for future openings.

The base salary range presented represents the anticipated low and high end salary range for new hires in this position. Your final base salary will be determined based on factors such as work location, experience, job related skills, and relevant training and education. The range listed is just one component of the total compensation package provided by Agero to employees.

National Pay Range: $110,000 USD - $135,000 USD

Life at Agero:

At Agero, you'll find a workplace where your unique perspective is not just welcomed, it's celebrated. We believe that our differences make us stronger, and we're committed to creating an environment where every employee feels a sense of belonging. If you're looking for a company that values your individuality, provides opportunities for growth, and champions open communication, Agero is the place for you. Join our team and help us drive the future of driver assistance, while experiencing a workplace where you can truly thrive.

Benefits Built for Well-being: 

Agero’s innovation is driven by a workforce where all associates feel like they can truly thrive. Agero offers a wide range of benefits to promote well-being, encourage personal development, and ensure financial stability. Our benefits include:

Health and Wellness: Healthcare, dental, vision, disability, life insurance, and mental health benefits for associates and their families.
Financial Security: 401(k) plan with company match and tuition assistance to support your future goals.
Work-Life Balance: Flexible time off, paid sick leave, and ten paid holidays annually.
For Contact Center Roles: Accrual of up to 3 weeks Paid Time Off per year, paid sick leave, and ten paid holidays annually.
Family Support: Parental planning benefits to assist associates through life’s milestones.
Bonus/Incentive Programs

Join Agero and experience a workplace that invests in your success both personally and professionally.
